subject: FinHealth pilot — can debug logs be retained for troubleshooting without risk of model training?
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: legal_ops@finhealth.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on debug logs + 'we do not train' claim

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Before we start the pilot, our security and legal teams want one last clarification: your standard "we do not train on customer data" statement sounds great, but we need to confirm operational nuances. Specifically: can we retain short-lived debug logs and a small number of anonymized stack traces for debugging (7–14 days) and still be covered by the non-training guarantee?

Also: are there any backend snapshots, backups, or telemetry flows that might be used for internal model improvement even if the customer data bucket is marked as "no-train"? If so, what controls can be applied (separate project IDs, encryption with customer KMS, deletion tombstones) so we can sign off?

If it helps, I can share a sample debug file — attaching a sanitized example.

Cheers,
Priya
Security Program Manager
FinHealth

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finhealth.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on debug logs + 'we do not train' claim

Thanks for the clear question, Priya — good one. Short answer: retaining short-lived debug artifacts for troubleshooting is compatible with our non-training guarantee provided certain controls are in place. Longer answer and the controls below.

High level assurances:
- Redwood does not use customer request/response text for ongoing model training or offline model updates by default for any customer who opts into the "no-model-training" setting.
- For customers on Dedicated/Private deployments we isolate logs and backups to customer-only storage and do not route telemetry into our internal training pipelines.

Operational caveats & required controls for the FinHealth pilot:
1) Scoped retention: Debug logs retained only in the project/container you designate (we recommend a dedicated S3 bucket or VPC-attached store). Default retention we can enforce is 7 days; you may request up to 14 days with written approval.
2) Processing flags: Any debug artifact uploaded with "no-train" metadata will be excluded from ingestion paths that feed our analytics/training systems. This is implemented as a routing metadata flag (no_train=true) at ingestion and enforced by the routing service.
3) Snapshot/backups: Automatic periodic snapshots (used for HA and failover) will be stored in a separate retention class tied to the customer project. For FinHealth pilot we can disable cross-customer snapshot consolidation and opt-out from internal snapshot-based analytics.
4) Encryption & keying: We offer customer-managed keys (KMS) for both runtime logs and snapshot storage; if you enable CMK, Redwood personnel cannot decrypt without a temporary key share that you approve.
5) Access & audit: All internal accesses to debug artifacts are logged and surfaced in the Console audit trail. We can add a limited-access role for the FinHealth SREs to review request-level guards.

I attached a short retention matrix (PDF) that shows where debug logs live and which controls apply. If you want, Mina can follow up with a sample RBAC configuration.

— Jonas
VP, Security & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention-matrix-v1.pdf
From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on debug logs + 'we do not train' claim

Priya — adding a couple concrete examples and the enforcement steps we will take for the pilot.

Example 1 — ephemeral request logs used to debug a tokenization edge case:
- Life cycle: captured at request time → marked no_train=true → stored in project-specific log bucket → auto-delete after 7 days.
- Enforcement: ingestion rule denies export to analytics/training queues; any attempt to lift the flag requires audit-logged approval.

Example 2 — HA snapshot created during maintenance window:
- Life cycle: saved as encrypted snapshot in your project → retention 30 days by default for HA, but we can reduce to 14 for pilot or disable cross-customer pinning.
- Enforcement: snapshots are tagged and excluded from aggregate telemetry exports.

Additional notes:
- Telemetry & aggregated stats (latency, CPU utilization) are derived metrics only; they do not contain raw customer text and are allowed for product improvement.
- We will provide a one-page attestation (signed by engineering + security) that the pilot configuration will not feed any customer text into model training systems. That attestation can be appended to the SOW.

If legal needs specific language, we can propose contract language clauses: a) explicit non-derivative clause, b) audit right for a one-time evidence review, c) CMK requirement.

Fwd: Marissa, Sean — can you confirm we can lock the project-level retention to 7 days and produce the attestation this week?

Thanks, Mina
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Priya — confirming operational commitments for the pilot:
- We will enforce a project-isolated log bucket and a default 7-day auto-delete for debug artifacts. If FinHealth signs the pilot SOW we will document the 14-day exception process.
- Redwood will deliver a signed technical attestation (engineering + security) describing the exclusion controls and a one-time evidence export (audit logs showing no export to training pipelines).
- CMK available on request; we will include CMK enablement steps as an appendix to the SOW.

Next steps for closing this item:
1) Priya/legal: confirm you accept the 7-day default and whether you want the 14-day process documented.
2) FinHealth: if you require CMK, send procurement contacts and we will add the CMK onboarding checklist to the SOW.
3) Redwood: we will attach the attestation and the RBAC snippet to the SOW and provide a HubSpot record link for the pilot.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if you want final sign-off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
